title: VISTA’s look at the Helix Nebula
caption: The Helix Nebula in infrared light, imaged by ESO's VISTA telescope
celestial: Helix Nebula, NGC 7293 · constellation Aquarius · about 700 light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESO/VISTA/J. Emerson. Acknowledgment: Cambridge Astronomical Survey Unit

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This unusual view of the Helix Nebula, also cataloged as NGC 7293, comes from ESO's Visible and Infrared Survey Telescope for Astronomy, known as VISTA. The Helix is a planetary nebula about 700 light-years away, and it is surrounded by a rich background of stars and galaxies.

A planetary nebula forms when a star like the Sun nears the end of its life and puffs its outer layers of gas out into space, where the hot core left behind makes them glow. Despite the name, planetary nebulae have nothing to do with planets.

VISTA observed the nebula in infrared light, and its infrared vision picks out strands of cold gas in the nebula that are mostly hidden in ordinary visible-light images of the Helix. It also reveals the many stars and galaxies in the background, giving a fuller picture of the nebula and its surroundings.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (37.51 x 37.51 arcminutes) and distance (700 light years), the frame spans roughly 7.6 × 7.6 light-years. Its light set out about 700 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This color picture was made by ESO's VISTA telescope and its VIRCAM camera from images taken through Y, J and K infrared filters. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
